summary: Redwood walkthrough of data handling and retention controls focusing on request storage toggles, PII redaction, and logging/audit options. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated/Private deployment for PCI-adjacent workloads; main concerns: PII redaction accuracy, ability to disable request retention per-route, and audit logs for compliance.
transcript: 00:00 Speaker 1 (Liam): Hey everyone, Liam Carter from Redwood, thanks for joining, um we wanted to run through our data handling controls and show the Console + API toggles for retention and redaction. 00:10 Speaker 2 (Aaron): Thanks Liam, Aaron Blake here. We're mostly worried about cardholder adjacent data and customer PII, we heard Redwood has per-route retention toggles and redaction, want to see how precise that is. 00:25 Speaker 3 (Maya): Hi this is Maya, Head of Security, I'll focus on encryption, audit trails, and whether we can ensure no raw requests land in long term storage. 00:40 Speaker 1 (Liam): Totally, that's the right set. Priya, feel free to jump in and demo the console. 00:45 Speaker 4 (Priya): Yep, hi all. So first slide is high level: three modes - hosted, dedicated, private. For PCI-adjacent we often recommend Private or Dedicated with VPC peering and KMS bring-your-own-key; but you can also use hosted with request-storage disabled. 01:10 Speaker 2 (Aaron): Quick question — if we disable request storage on hosted, how does debugging work? We'll need some traces for troubleshoot. 01:18 Speaker 4 (Priya): Good question. We have a couple options: short-lived ephemeral logs (30-day window) that can be rotated and automatically redacted, or we can enable request snapshotting only for specific routes or sessions. There's also structured metrics and sampling to reduce the surface area. 01:35 Speaker 3 (Maya): When you say redaction, is that ML-based PII detection or rules? We need deterministic guarantees for certain fields. 01:42 Speaker 4 (Priya): It's a hybrid. We use deterministic field-based masking (e.g., regexes for card numbers, emails) + ML PII detection for free-text. You can configure blacklist/whitelist fields per route. For high-compliance customers we recommend rules-first plus detection as guardrails. 02:05 Speaker 2 (Aaron): Do you keep a copy of the original unredacted payload anywhere? 02:09 Speaker 1 (Liam): Short answer: no for standard hosted when request-storage is off. For dedicated/private there are configuration options: you can disable persistence entirely and keep only in-memory caches for KV for the duration of the request; otherwise we persist masked/hashed traces and full payloads only if you opt in. 02:27 Speaker 3 (Maya): We also need audit logs for admin actions and redaction changes, who changed retention. 02:33 Speaker 4 (Priya): Audit logs are available as an immutable stream — we can forward to your cloud logging (S3, CloudWatch, GCS) or provide a read-only audit view in Console. All admin actions, policy changes, and retention toggles are logged with actor and timestamp. 02:50 Speaker 5 (Jon): Jon Park — from infra, curious about the API: how do we toggle retention via API vs Console? Is it per-route or per-model? 02:58 Speaker 4 (Priya): You can do both. There's a per-route config object in the API: retention_enabled: true/false, retention_window_days: N, redaction_policy: [rules], storage_tier: [hot|cold|none]. We'll show the console UI for the same controls so you can script it in infra or set it in UI. 03:20 Speaker 1 (Liam): Priya, can you show the demo tenant now? 03:23 Speaker 4 (Priya): Sure sharing screen — Console > Projects > Montecito-Pilot. Top right is Tenant settings, then Data Handling. 03:30 Speaker 4 (Priya): (typing) Here we have toggles: Request storage: Enabled / Disabled; Default retention window: 90 days; Per-route overrides. I'm going to flip request storage to Disabled for the payments-route and show that the API returns a masked copy to us but no raw payload stored. 03:50 Speaker 2 (Aaron): Ok show the logs after the change so we can see what a stored object looks like when masked. 03:55 Speaker 4 (Priya): Loading logs — here's sample: timestamp, route, model, masked_request: {"user_input":"[REDACTED_EMAIL] transferred $[REDACTED_CARD]"}, redaction_meta: {"rules_applied":["cc_regex","email_regex"],"detector_confidence":0.87}. Note: transcript sometimes shows field names screwed up in export — but internal we keep JSON. 04:20 Speaker 3 (Maya): That redaction_meta, can we push that to our SIEM? We need to show redaction proof for audits. 04:26 Speaker 4 (Priya): Yep, it's included in the audit export — you get event with redaction hashes and applied rules, timestamps, and actor. We can forward via webhook or S3 with lifecycle. 04:38 Speaker 5 (Jon): For performance, does enabling redaction add latency? We run latency-sensitive flows. 04:43 Speaker 4 (Priya): Minimal — deterministic regexes are negligible. ML PII detection runs asynchronously for non-blocking, but we offer sync redaction if you need stronger guarantees and don't mind ~10-40ms overhead depending on model and sequence length. 05:00 Speaker 2 (Aaron): And can we do per-model retention? Like some models we want to keep for fine-tuning, others no. 05:06 Speaker 1 (Liam): Yes — retention targets can be set per-route or per-model, and we also support lifecycle policies: auto-delete after N days, cold-archive for X days, or redact then archive. 05:20 Speaker 3 (Maya): How about encryption-at-rest, KMS, and BYOK? 05:24 Speaker 4 (Priya): Support for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports provider-managed keys but you can request a dedicated key for enterprise deals. All data at rest is encrypted, and transit uses TLS. 05:38 Speaker 2 (Aaron): In the case we pick hosted but want absolute no-retention, how do we prove there is no copy in backups? 05:45 Speaker 1 (Liam): We can provide an architecture diagram and describe the retention flows, plus a statement for the pilot config. For legal you can get contract language restricting retention and a technical attestation for pilot. For Dedicated/Private you get more control. 06:05 Speaker 3 (Maya): Are there any known gaps? e.g., system logs that might include request identifiers or truncated content? 06:13 Speaker 4 (Priya): We do capture operational traces and request IDs for debugging; those can be set to obfuscated/hashed and excluded from long-term logs on request. We recommend a policy: obfuscate request ID + sample traces for 7-30 days. 06:30 Speaker 5 (Jon): About integrations — we'll want audit exports into our ELK stack; is that straightforward? 06:35 Speaker 4 (Priya): Yes we have connectors: S3 export + Lambda to push to ES, direct CloudWatch or GCS sinks, and webhooks for event streams. 06:45 Speaker 2 (Aaron): What's the path to pilot? timeline? 06:48 Speaker 1 (Liam): Typical: 2-week pilot, test 3-5 routes, validate redaction on sample prompts, validate that retention toggles behave as expected, and then we discuss Dedicated vs Hosted SLOs. Priya will spin up a tenant and share sample configs. 07:05 Speaker 3 (Maya): For compliance we'll need a runbook for incident response related to data exposures. 07:10 Speaker 4 (Priya): We'll include a runbook template in the security packet. 07:15 Speaker 2 (Aaron): Any limitations on PII detector? False positives/negatives? 07:20 Speaker 4 (Priya): There are edge cases — we provide evaluation metrics and you can feed redaction test sets; Redwood Optimize can recommend rule updates and catch regressions over time. 07:35 Speaker 1 (Liam): Quick note on pricing: retention and storage tier affect unit cost; cold archive reduces cost but still counted for compliance; we'll include a cost example in the follow-up. 07:50 Speaker 5 (Jon): Ok one last technical: if we run Private, can we host the audit logs on-prem only? 07:55 Speaker 4 (Priya): Yes, Private supports on-prem log sinks and air-gapped options. 08:02 Speaker 3 (Maya): Thanks, that helps. Recap next steps? 08:06 Speaker 1 (Liam): Recap: we'll send security docs, Priya will provision demo tenant and sample retention configs, Montecito to confirm pilot routes and in-scope PII. 08:15 Speaker 2 (Aaron): Sounds good, thanks everyone. 08:18 Speaker 1 (Liam): Thanks all. End call.
